rationale: Round-4 zero-ask regression check of 6cdac6e5 in my grounding lens. ALL THREE assigned targets verify against the tree. (1) The recordMergeSourceMarker precedent is REAL: internal/gitutil/gitops.go:211 defines it, :187 builds the ref name under `refs/mindspec/merge-source/<source>`, call sites at :259/:284, with the spec-127 bead-6 attribution in the comment at :221 — so `refs/mindspec/materialized/<bead-id>` is a sibling subnamespace of an established house pattern, and homing the new helpers in internal/gitutil beside the precedent (bead 6 step 4) is the right seam. The trust class also matches the precedent: merge_resumption.go:221's own comment acknowledges in-repo markers cannot defend against local tampering, and the resume design claims no more than 127's markers do — the ≠tip path deletes the stale marker and re-runs with stale-SHA evaluating as today, so no foreign commit is laundered through the STALE path, and the ==tip path's provenance guarantee is the same same-machine trust class 127 already ships. (2) The neteffect precedent is REAL: internal/gitutil/neteffect.go exists and its :747 comment states the 'unreferenced loose tree objects' non-mutating discipline (echoed at workdestruction.go:620) — the G6 qualification (refused gate leaves ref/tip/tracker/real-index/worktree unchanged; unreachable gc-collectable loose objects from write-tree/commit-tree may exist) is exactly what the plumbing produces, and since the marker ref is written only after all gates pass, a refusal leaves no ref either — the qualified guarantee is precise and true. (3) Chunk-vs-section sweep spot-checked on chunks 1, 2, and 6: chunk 1 now carries all nine writer files + the lock/order/inventory files + repair + the sweep-found .gitignore, matching bead 1's steps exactly; chunk 2 carries the value-semantics files + semantics_v2 + the panel-added impl.go and repair.go, matching bead 2 (including the round-3 invocation-site additions); chunk 6 carries snapshot/executor/validate/complete/ADR-0041 files and gitops.go, which now also homes the marker helpers — consistent. Beyond the assigned targets I re-derived the resume-detection crash windows: marker-before-update-ref is load-bearing (a crash between update-ref and reset leaves marker==tip==C, so the plain re-run resumes forward instead of wedging on stale-SHA against the tool's own commit — the exact hole a marker-after-update-ref ordering would reopen), the stale path (marker≠tip) degrades to today's behavior, and skipping the step-2.26 work-destruction preflight in resume mode is safe by the code's own architecture (complete.go:780-783: that preflight is a convenience early-refusal; the executor's live consultation immediately before MergeInto is the authoritative gate). The G3 Windows replacement (LockFileEx on a retained handle, no FILE_SHARE_DELETE) is grounded in real OS semantics — kernel-held, death-releasing, owner-only — and by deleting the stale-file design entirely it also moots my round-3 minor finding R2-3-3 (the verify-once overclaim): delete-over-patch, correctly applied. ONE minor internal inconsistency introduced by this commit, non-blocking: bead 6 step 4's compressed arrow list orders the op '(marker-ref write → commit-tree from T → …)', but the marker's VALUE is C, which does not exist until commit-tree runs — the authoritative protocol paragraph has the correct order (commit-tree creates C; the marker = C is written immediately before the update-ref, after every gate passed). The literal step-4 order is unimplementable on its face (no SHA to write), so it cannot mislead an implementer past the protocol paragraph and fixture (viii); it is a wording slip, not a design defect. Recording it for a one-line fold-in whenever the plan file is next touched; it does not warrant a round on its own.

findings.claim: All three assigned regression targets verified TRUE.
findings.evidence: recordMergeSourceMarker at gitops.go:211 with refs/mindspec/merge-source/ at :187 and spec-127 attribution at :221 (marker-ref namespace precedent holds); neteffect.go:747 + workdestruction.go:620 'unreferenced loose tree objects' discipline (G6's gc-collectable qualification precise); chunks 1/2/6 vs bead sections 1/2/6 consistent including the sweep additions (.gitignore, impl.go, repair.go) and gitops.go homing the marker helpers.

findings.claim: Bead 6 step 4's arrow list '(marker-ref write → commit-tree from T → expected-old-tip update-ref → index-only reset)' contradicts the protocol paragraph's order.
findings.evidence: The marker's value IS C (`refs/mindspec/materialized/<bead-id>` = C), so commit-tree must precede the marker write; the protocol paragraph states this correctly ('immediately before the update-ref … only after every gate has passed'). The step-4 restatement lists the marker write first — literally unimplementable (no SHA exists yet), so it cannot silently mislead, but the two passages disagree.
findings.disposition: Non-blocking wording slip: fold a one-line reorder of the step-4 parenthetical (commit-tree → marker write → update-ref → reset) into the next touch of plan.md; the protocol paragraph and fixture (viii) are the authoritative statements and are correct.

findings.claim: My round-3 minor finding R2-3-3 (Windows post-create-verify 'closes the interleave' overclaim) is MOOT.
findings.evidence: 6cdac6e5 deletes the stale-file takeover design entirely in favor of LockFileEx on a retained handle (no FILE_SHARE_DELETE): ownership and atomicity are the OS's, crashed holders release with the process, and the stale-FILE class no longer exists (a leftover empty/partial file never blocks). The barrier-controlled two-contender test subsumes the interleave concern.
